intro: Firefighting builds coordination, quick judgment and care for people in crisis. Of the 25 careers below, the closest by skills is Forest and Conservation Workers at a 74% match, while the best-paid close move is fire supervision: First-Line Supervisors of Firefighting and Prevention Workers earn a BLS May 2025 median of $93,530, or 58% more.
why_it_works: On a call you coordinate with a crew, size up danger and help people at their worst moment. O*NET rates coordination at 3.88 out of 5 for firefighters, one of the highest scores on any public safety page. That team discipline fits rail, transit and vessel operation jobs. Most matches need no extra schooling. The gaps are leading people and running or repairing machinery.
tips: Count your certifications, such as EMT, hazmat or driver-operator; each one opens a different path.
Transit is a quiet surprise: Subway and Streetcar Operators earn $86,380, which is 46% more than firefighters.
If you want to stay in fire service, ask about inspector or prevention roles before leaving the department.

faq.q: What jobs can former firefighters do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Forest and Conservation Workers (74%), fire supervisors (73%) and Subway and Streetcar Operators (73%), based on O*NET 31.0. Bridge and Lock Tenders are also 72% matched, with a median of $57,700, which is 3% less than the $59,280 firefighter median.

faq.q: Which careers for former firefighters pay more?
faq.a: 12 of the 25 matches pay more than firefighting. Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers earn $95,320 (61% more), fire supervisors $93,530 (58% more) and water vessel captains, mates and pilots $92,460 (56% more), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do firefighters need a degree for a second career?
faq.a: Usually not. 21 of the 25 matches need no more education than firefighters already have. In the closest match, 44% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent. Supervisor and vessel roles usually call for a certificate or license instead.

faq.q: What skills should firefighters learn for a new job?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing people, operation and control, operations monitoring and repairing. Judgment and service orientation already rate 3.5 out of 5 for firefighters in O*NET, so the step is usually technical training, not people skills.
